name: Coordinated Inauthentic Behavior
description: Detection and analysis of coordinated link-sharing, inauthentic networks, and deceptive information operations on social media platforms, the core methodological signature of Giglietto's research (CooRnet/CLSB, VERA-AI Alert, Facebook network studies). Central to his current work as WP4 leader on vera.ai and ongoing monitoring projects.

name: Information Disorder & Misinformation
description: Broad research line on the spread, taxonomy, and mitigation of fake news, disinformation, and problematic information across hybrid media systems, spanning topics from Charlie Hebdo hashtag studies to the PROMPT project on disinformation narratives in Europe (Ukraine war, LGBTQI+ rights, elections).

name: Generative AI & Synthetic Media
description: Study of generative AI's role in disinformation and persuasion, including AI-generated visual content in coordinated gambling promotion and the new master's course 'IA Generativa e Media'; reflects a growing current-agenda emphasis on AI-driven manipulation and countermeasures.

name: LLMs & Computational Content Analysis
description: Methodological work integrating large language models and embedding techniques into content classification, annotation, and political discourse analysis, including validation of LLM-in-the-loop pipelines and comparative embedding studies for Italian political news.

name: Platform Governance & Research Data Access
description: Research and policy engagement on social media platforms' data-access regimes, API infrastructures, and content moderation policies under the EU Digital Services Act, including analyses of Meta's URL Shares Dataset, political content reduction policy, and service as a JRC/ECAT independent expert.

name: Political Polarization & Partisanship
description: Analysis of partisan community dynamics, affective polarization, and cross-partisan versus insular media engagement on social platforms, spanning Italian, Brazilian, and Latin American contexts and informing key-concept debates in digital media research.

name: Elections & Social Media Campaigns
description: Empirical mapping of political communication, coordinated networks, and news circulation around national elections (Italy 2018/2022, Germany 2021, Brazil), the founding empirical domain of the MINE research programme.

name: Health Misinformation & Problematic Content
description: Investigation of coordinated networks spreading problematic health information, including COVID-19 fact-checking acceleration and cross-national studies of health misinformation circulation in India and Nigeria funded by the Gates Foundation.

name: Digital Research Methods & Tools
description: Development and dissemination of open-source computational tools and workflows for social media research, including CooRnet, CooRTweet's underlying CLSB methodology, and teaching materials (R/Python tutorials) supporting reproducible digital methods.

name: Platforms, Audiences, and Online Communities
description: Empirical and reflective studies of how platform affordances, cultures, and audience practices shape online sociality, identity, and community formation across sites like Facebook, TikTok, Instagram, Twitter/Mastodon, and LiveJournal.

name: Critical Analysis of AI Industry Imaginaries and Discourse
description: Studies examining how AI industry actors, media, and communities construct and circulate narratives, imaginaries, and framings (e.g., longtermism, techno-hagiography, 'quiet futuring', political-economy 'decoys') that shape public understanding and obscure or legitimize the underlying power structures of AI development.

name: Reflections on the State of Misinformation and Online Harm Research
description: Papers that step back from primary empirical study to critically assess the misinformation/online-harms research field itself — diagnosing biases (e.g., WEIRD-centrism, overreliance on cognitive proxies), mapping gaps in evidence (causal, longitudinal, cross-national), and proposing directions or borrowed lessons (e.g., from climate psychology) to make the field more rigorous and generalizable.

name: Theorizing AI's Social Role: Agency, Trust, and Public Perception
description: Papers that apply or extend social theory and communication-trust frameworks to understand the societal position of AI systems, ranging from conceptual demarcations of machine agency and formal multi-agent social frameworks to models of public trust in generative AI and empirical survey data on public attitudes toward AI adoption.

name: Computational Studies of Political Media and Advertising
description: Papers using large-scale computational or quasi-experimental methods to study political advertising, media capture, and ideological signaling on digital platforms, including causal analysis of ad effects, detection of covert advertiser influence on news coverage, and latent ideology estimation of political video content.
